newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises to 10.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises to 10.1 percent.

text.p: Average lending rate rose to 10.1 percent on Monday from 9.6 percent Friday after long-term loans moved to higher rates.
Total settlements were 76.1 million kuna, of which 22.2 million accounted for fresh kuna loans.
Most borrowings were made at the call money rate of 9.4 percent while longer-term loans ranged between 15 and 20 percent.
Weekend overnight trade totalled a meagre 5.1 million kuna as only three banks with shorfalls squared their positions.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Tuesday were slightly firmer at 5.4928 to the dollar and 3.5621 to the German mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
